correctness.rationale: Positive diagonal pair-loss operator D implies every nondecaying H−iD/2 eigenmode is a real-energy H eigenvector with zero collision amplitude; the orthogonal reducing complement decays. In normalized boson basis, the leaf collision equations force hub-leaf coefficients a_i=0, the remaining leaf-pair equations force energy zero and Bc=0. For q>=3, the kernel of B^T would require u_i/w_i+u_j/w_j=0 on each pair; any triangle forces all u_i=0, so rank B=q and dark dimension binom(q,2)−q=q(q−3)/2. The displayed full orthogonal kernel projector and loss eta=1−tr(Pρ) follow; uniform hopping gives 2/(q−1) for a localized leaf pair. Independently constructed the q=4 weighted B with w=(1,2,3,4), verified full rank and the specific exact first-pair loss 179/929 by rational Gram inversion. The supplied separate two-body observability script checks finite instances, not the proof of all q or all positive γ_v.
residual_risks: All γ_v and all w_i must be strictly positive; q=2, detunings and direct leaf hopping are outside the stated theorem.

The q=4 sharp threshold, full weighted kernel projector and exact initial-pair capture law distinguish protected from unprotected two-boson configurations at all positive loss rates. This is a reusable structural classification of a nontrivial invariant subspace rather than only a finite simulation or a trivial type check.
